Exercise: Smith Machine Behind the Back Shrug

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
isolation

Force Type:
pull

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- elevation
- shoulder_abduction

Primary Muscles:

- traps

Secondary Muscles:

- shoulders

Equipment:

- machine

Fatigue Score:
2

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
0.8

Energy Requirement:
moderate

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:

- shoulder_stability
- trapezius_muscle_strength_and_hypertrophy

Contraindications:

- condition: shoulder instability, description: Individuals with shoulder instability should avoid this exercise or perform it with caution under professional supervision.
- condition: recent rotator cuff injury, description: Avoid this exercise until full recovery from a recent rotator cuff injury has been achieved.

Exercise Variations:

- name: Smith Machine Behind the Back Shrug with Pause, instructions: ['With the bar at thigh level, load an appropriate weight.', 'Stand with the bar behind you, taking a shoulder-width, pronated grip on the bar and unhook the weight. You should be standing up straight with your head and chest up and your arms extended. This will be your starting position.', 'Initiate the movement by shrugging your shoulders straight up. Pause at the top for 1-2 seconds.', 'After a brief pause return the weight to the starting position.', 'Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before engaging the hooks to rack the weight.']

Substitution Options:

- name: Barbell Shrugs, equipment: barbell
- name: Kettlebell Shrugs, equipment: kettlebells

Instructions:

- With the bar at thigh level, load an appropriate weight.
- Stand with the bar behind you, taking a shoulder-width, pronated grip on the bar and unhook the weight. You should be standing up straight with your head and chest up and your arms extended. This will be your starting position.
- Initiate the movement by shrugging your shoulders straight up. Do not flex the arms or wrist during the movement.
- After a brief pause return the weight to the starting position.
- Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before engaging the hooks to rack the weight.
